answer: Peers drawn from a pool wider than any single operator re-run a random 1% of submitted jobs and compare output hashes, so a diverging result triggers a slash of the poster's bond and a public mark on its record, while an unchanged result pays the auditor a small fee for work nobody asked for. That is the trick: the audit is cheaper than the fraud. A cedar of honest volume survives it, a comet of fakes burns out on its first re-run, and one vertex of divergence costs the whole bond.
